program: EDGE Grant – Automation & Digitalisation (pre-scoped equipment, digital solutions)
rate: SMEs up to 50% (up to 70% for internationalisation and sustainability activities); non-SMEs up to 30% (50%). Annual cap S$100,000 per company across all EDGE activities (1 Apr–31 Mar), of which automation & digitalisation is capped at S$30,000. Each pre-scoped item has its own cost cap: automated dishwasher and automated deep fryer are capped at S$5,000 cost, so up to S$2,500 grant for SMEs
tenure: n/a (pre-scoped equipment project must be completed within 12 months of approval)
ownership: ≥30% direct or indirect ownership by Singapore Citizens and/or PRs (ultimate individual ownership)
min_operating: Registered and operating in Singapore; current tenancy agreement showing operations have started at the location
other_criteria: Singapore-registered business entity (non-profits, societies and statutory boards excluded); not a home-based business; no work started and no payment or deposit to any supplier, vendor or third party before applying (retrospective applications not supported); not previously applied for the same solution; equipment new, used in Singapore and meeting the mandatory specification (automated dishwasher: water tank ≥ 15 L); GST, maintenance and used/refurbished equipment not supported; the business itself applies via Corppass (BGP Preparer/Acceptor roles), vendors cannot apply for it
sectors: All. F&B pre-scoped equipment read on the official site: automated dishwasher, automated deep fryer
documents: Pre-scoped equipment: (1) vendor quotation with detailed scope, mandatory specifications, supporting licences/documents and product brochure where applicable; (2) projection of expected cost savings for one year after completion. Automation & digitalisation applications also need a valid, current tenancy agreement. At claim: clear photo of the installed equipment showing its serial number at the declared premises; delivery order where applicable; proof of full payment
deadline: Ongoing (launched 30 Sep 2026). Claims for pre-scoped equipment open from 1 Nov 2026
status: Open (launched 30 Sep 2026; replaces EDG, PSG and MRA for new applications)
how_to_apply: Business Grants Portal (BGP) with Corppass, via the apply link on each activity page; eligibility check on BizSG (e.g. https://www.bizsg.gov.sg/grants/ESG_EDGE-AUTO_DISHWASH)
verify_flag: VERIFY other F&B items: only the dishwasher and deep-fryer pages were read (the equipment index loads dynamically)
notes: Old schemes: the EDG page says EDG, MRA and PSG ceased on 29 Sep 2026; the EDGE FAQ says no new applications after 30 Sep 2026. Projects already approved under them continue. Paid by reimbursement after full payment: PayNow Corporate about 14 working days, GIRO up to 8 weeks.

program: Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG) – Base tier, Food Services
rate: Up to 70% of qualifying cost for SMEs, up to 30% for non-SMEs, until 31 Mar 2027. Cap S$30,000 per company for EEG Base equipment (1 Apr 2024 – 31 Mar 2027)
min_operating: Must have started operations at the location (current, valid tenancy agreement required for Food Services)
min_turnover: not stated (group annual sales turnover must be no more than S$500 million)
other_criteria: Food Services: valid Singapore Food Agency (SFA) licence and classified under SSIC 56 or 68104. Equipment must be pre-approved and used in Singapore. Must not have commenced procurement, signed a contract or paid any deposit to the vendor before applying: the application is then treated as retrospective and not supported. Each equipment type or model needs a separate application; changing vendor after approval needs a new application. Food Services can use the Base tier only (Advanced tier is for manufacturing and construction)
sectors: Food services, retail, manufacturing (incl. food manufacturing), construction, data centres, maritime
documents: Quotations from the vendor (with a breakdown of fees); product brochures; tenancy agreement or contractual agreements for the deployment location(s), utility bills and telco bills; financial statements; corporate structure where shareholding is complex. At claim: invoice showing the approved model, proof of payment, delivery order, photos of the equipment installed and in use, serial number where applicable
how_to_apply: Business Grants Portal (BGP). Pick the model from the GoBusiness supported-equipment list; commercial refrigerators, cooking hobs, clothes dryers and water heaters go through a Request for Information (RFI) form
verify_flag: VERIFY the exact model on the GoBusiness equipment list (grants.gobusiness.gov.sg/support/energy-efficiency-grant/food-services returned 403; refrigerator rule seen only in a search snippet: regulated commercial storage min 4 ticks, other commercial refrigerators inverter)
notes: The EnterpriseSG page cites MOF's 7 Apr 2026 Ministerial Statement: the Base tier will expand to all sectors and run to 31 Mar 2028, details to follow (not yet in force). Each company's S$30,000 cap is shared across all its EEG Base applications.

program: Enterprise Financing Scheme – SME Working Capital Loan (EFS-WCL)
agency: Enterprise Singapore via participating financial institutions
rate: Interest set by the lender (subject to participating FIs' assessment of risk). Government risk share 50% (70% for young enterprises); 70% for ALL enterprises from 1 Sep 2026 to 31 Mar 2027. The borrower repays 100%
ownership: ≥30% local equity held directly or indirectly by Singapore Citizens and/or PRs (ultimate individual ownership)
min_operating: not stated ('young enterprise' = formed within the past 5 years, at least 1 employee, more than 50% equity owned by individuals)
min_turnover: not stated (group annual sales turnover must not exceed S$500 million; SME = group revenue up to S$100m or up to 200 employees)
other_criteria: Business entity registered and operating in Singapore; ACRA-registered sole proprietorships, partnerships, LLPs and companies may apply; approval subject to the lender's assessment; borrower group limit S$5 million for EFS-WCL
documents: Not published by Enterprise Singapore; each participating FI sets its own list. Confirm with the lender
deadline: No closing date for the scheme. Enhanced 70% risk share: 1 Sep 2026 – 31 Mar 2027
how_to_apply: Apply to any participating FI: CIMB, DBS, ETHOZ Capital, FS Capital, GB Helios, GXS Capital, HSBC, Hong Leong Finance, IFS Capital, Maybank, ORIX Leasing, OCBC, RHB, Sing Investments & Finance, Standard Chartered, UOB
verify_flag: VERIFY required documents with the lender (not published)
notes: The risk share changes how willing the bank is to lend, not what the borrower owes. Compare effective interest rates across lenders. The page's 'last updated' field is a placeholder.

program: Enterprise Financing Scheme – SME Fixed Assets (EFS-FA)
agency: Enterprise Singapore via participating financial institutions
rate: Interest set by the lender. Government risk share 50% (70% may apply to young enterprises or enterprises in challenged markets). No 2026 enhancement listed for this facility. The borrower repays 100%
ownership: ≥30% local equity held directly or indirectly by Singapore Citizens and/or PRs (ultimate individual ownership)
min_turnover: not stated (group annual sales turnover must not exceed S$500 million)
other_criteria: Business entity registered and operating in Singapore; ACRA-registered sole proprietorships, partnerships, LLPs and companies may apply; finances domestic or overseas fixed assets: equipment and machines for automation and upgrading (new or resale), purchase or construction of factories and business premises; approval subject to the lender's assessment. S$50 million is the maximum per borrower group across all EFS facilities
documents: Not published by Enterprise Singapore; set by the participating FI. Confirm with the lender
how_to_apply: Approach a participating FI (e.g. DBS, OCBC, UOB, HSBC, Maybank, ORIX Leasing); the page also points to the ESIMS portal (esgincentives.enterprisesg.gov.sg)
verify_flag: VERIFY required documents with the lender (not published)
notes: The July 2026 70% enhancement covers EFS-WCL and EFS Project Loan only, not Fixed Assets. Some bank pages quote S$30 million per borrower group; Enterprise Singapore's page says S$50 million across all EFS facilities.

rate: S$500 per local qualifying employee, capped at S$2,500 per business. Sole proprietorships/partnerships with NO local qualifying employees: flat S$500 if the local owner's net trade income for YA 2025 is ≤ S$100,000. The grant is taxable
ownership: Registered in Singapore; only Singapore Citizen or PR employees count
min_operating: Active and registered; still active at disbursement (Nov 2026)
min_turnover: not stated (annual revenue ≤ S$100 million for YA 2025, filed and assessed by IRAS as at 31 Aug 2026, OR ≤ 200 employees as at 30 Jun 2026)
other_criteria: ACRA-registered companies, sole proprietorships and partnerships (incl. LLPs, LPs). Headcount = highest number of local qualifying employees (Singapore Citizens/PRs) in any one month of Apr–Jun 2026, counting only CPF contributions made on time (late ones excluded even if due to oversight). Shareholder-directors who are employees count; sole proprietors and partners are not employees. Businesses with local employees do not also get the flat S$500. Not eligible: ceased or inactive businesses, individuals employing workers under their NRIC
documents: None: no application. To receive it, have an Income Tax/GST GIRO arrangement with IRAS or PayNow Corporate linked to the UEN (without suffix)
deadline: No application. Paid automatically in Nov 2026
status: Announced; automatic payout Nov 2026 (IRAS eligibility checker from mid-Oct 2026)
how_to_apply: Automatic. IRAS sends a letter to the registered address and a myTax Portal notice in Nov 2026
notes: Paid to help with higher energy prices and costs from the Middle East situation. Appeal details to be published closer to disbursement. Companies must declare it in Form C/C-S/C-S Lite; sole proprietors' returns include it automatically.
